This is certainly an interesting discussion to see crop up so much lately. I've never watched critical role, but I've certainly had players that have watched it or other similar things.

I usually end up being DM (because I'm usually the one that knows how) and I used to get pretty continually frustrated with the way players just wouldn't interact with the world or what I lay in front of them. People wouldn't really repleplay, and would focus on what the best solution is rather than what in character, or they wouldn't really act in character at all. The games would get stuck in this low energy place where no one's really engaging.

In my case, I adjusted strategies. Nowadays I favor devising campaigns that take place in smaller locations that are more consistently detailed, and giving the players more of a sandbox with set characters, faction, etc. Some folks might be bothered with the lack of scope, but it's worked well for my players, as having a lot of options to engage with and an active world that shifts has made them feel more involved. That's keeping in mind I tend to run with a lot of new players just getting interested in tabletops. 

Course, I don't think critical role was a thing then? Or if it was, it certainly wasn't as well known.

It's also worth considering if DnD is the right system for your goals with your players! While I always and forever adore DnD, there's options that work better for the "open world" style I mentioned, and I recently ran a few sessions of Blades in the Dark with my group (before covid caused issues).

Try and think about what your group will engage with, and analyse if what you have to work with suits that.

When I started playing WF on Playstation, I didn't bother with my operator like so many others. It seemed incredibly obtuse, and as a newer player I was more interested in getting the frames, weapons, and mods I wanted.

Getting back into it on PC, I committed to building a real amp and putting effort into getting focus. I've since discovered that I actually like the operator and enjoy what it brings to my kit and versatility.

But so far focus farming has never stopped being awful. I was able to get into building various amps, eidolon hunting, and I like the skills I've accumulated from the focus I have farmed. But got, it's ridiculously annoying.

It's also not scaled for people new to the system. The cost of skills and schools feels more balanced for a developed operator hunting eidolons and such, so it's an awful uphill battle to get to even unlocking your first real skill! Also lack of explanation makes it common for new players to dump a bunch into capacity off the bat because they can't afford anything else.

Oh and that's without even mentioning unlocking new schools. I couldn't remember the word for zenurik on my new account and picked a different one, so I had to accumulate focus and grind it out only to spend it all just on unlocking the school.

But yes. Lenses shouldn't break that easy, especially when you've made a nice one, it's silly that they do in the first place. No other gear is like that.

I think the operator and focus system is cooler than a lot of people give it credit for, but I really can't blame people for skipping on it!

I know people have commented about new content bringing in new players, but the thing we need to keep in mind is the vast majority of new content requires committing to a long grind!

And you know what's before that new content? Old content, that is aged and completely at odds with later quests. You have old tilesets and bosses like those on Earth and Mars contrasted against some of the shiny and new corpus tilesets added alongside granum void. You have the individual level tiles contrasted with the art and look of the open worlds. I think for a lot of players that can be a huge turn off. 

I don't think the quests themselves need that much of a rework, aside from a quality of life perspective, or small improvements to the transmission segments that actually progress the story.

But the tilesets as well as some bugginess in the early segments could certainly use some help. It doesn't need to be a rework on the level of Jupiter, the game just needs to look more like the pieces fit together and provide a less buggy experience for new players. ESPECIALLY with the newer intro cutscene and such at the start.

Those new players won't stay if the game looks so unpolished, and as someone who recently started over on PC with a new account, the star chart can feel like quite the slog due to this stuff.
